record.what_it_does: Snowflake is a cloud data platform (data warehouse, data lake, and AI/app development platform) that can be controlled and queried programmatically via REST APIs.
record.auth_notes: Snowflake's SQL API and REST APIs accept a Bearer token that can be an OAuth2 access token, a key-pair JWT, a Programmatic Access Token (a static bearer token), or a workload-identity-federation token (AWS/Azure/GCP/OIDC). OAuth2 (Snowflake OAuth or External OAuth via an IdP like Okta/Entra) is the method intended for third-party/multi-user clients, including the official MCP server which uses OAuth by default.
record.access_notes: Anyone can sign up for a 30-day free trial with $400 in credits and immediately get an account plus API/OAuth credentials to build against; there is no perpetual free tier, so sustained use requires converting to a paid account.
record.main_blocker: Free access is trial-only (30 days); production use requires a paid Snowflake account, and per-customer setup (warehouse, roles, security integration) is needed for each user.
